title: Ensure All Default Passwords Are Changed
description: Default passwords should not be used by Oracle database users. Leaving default passwords unchanged can create significant security vulnerabilities by allowing unauthorized access to the database. Counts every account listed in CDB_USERS_WITH_DEFPWD, locked or not, as the benchmark does. Run on the database host as the Oracle software owner with ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_SID and PATH set; connects to the CDB root with 'sqlplus -S / as sysdba' (OS authentication) so CDB_/GV$ views cover all open PDBs.
reference: CIS Oracle Database 23ai Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1 Ensure All Default Passwords Are Changed

audit.command:
out=$(sqlplus -S -L / as sysdba 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
whenever sqlerror exit failure
set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off
select count(*) from cdb_users_with_defpwd a, cdb_users c
where a.username = c.username and a.con_id = c.con_id;
exit
EOF
) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: To reset the account with NO AUTHENTICATION, execute the following SQL statement in CDB: ALTER USER <USERNAME> NO AUTHENTICATION; Notes: ; As per Oracle Support Document 2173962.1, newly created database may list SYS and SYSTEM in CBA_USERS_WITH_DEFPWD even if they were set with non- default passwords. Running ALTER USER with the same password will correctly recognize these accounts as non-default. ; If remote_password_file is set to NONE, changing the SYS password via ALTER USER is not possible. In this case, update remote_password_file to EXCLUSIVE before modifying the SYS password.

title: Ensure 'REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT' is set to FALSE
description: TRUE trusts the client's operating-system user name for OPS$ accounts, which any remote host can spoof. If the parameter no longer exists in the release it is treated as FALSE. Run on the database host as the Oracle software owner with ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_SID and PATH set; connects with 'sqlplus -S / as sysdba' (OS authentication).
reference: CIS Oracle Database 19c Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.3.14 Ensure 'REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT' Is Set to 'FALSE' (not in the 23ai v1.1.0 benchmark; the parameter is desupported there)

audit.command:
out=$(sqlplus -S -L / as sysdba 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
whenever sqlerror exit failure
set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on
select nvl((select upper(value) from v$parameter where name = 'remote_os_authent'), 'FALSE') from dual;
exit
EOF
) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: ALTER SYSTEM SET REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT = FALSE SCOPE = SPFILE; then restart the instance (rolling restart on RAC)

For example, on Linux systems: opatch lsinventory | grep -e "^.*<latest_patch_version_number>\s*.*$" For example, on Windows systems: opatch lsinventory | find "<latest_patch_version_number>"

title: Ensure 'extproc' Is Not Present In 'listener.ora'
description: extproc should be removed from the listener.ora to mitigate the risk that OS libraries can be invoked by the Oracle instance. Passes when listener.ora contains no extproc entry (or no listener.ora exists in that directory). 19c v2.0.0 titles this "Ensure 'extproc' Is Not Enabled". Reads the file from $TNS_ADMIN, or $ORACLE_HOME/network/admin when TNS_ADMIN is unset (Linux/UNIX hosts); fails when neither directory exists.
reference: CIS Oracle Database 23ai Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.1 Ensure 'extproc' Is Not Present In 'listener.ora'

audit.command: d="${TNS_ADMIN:-${ORACLE_HOME:?ORACLE_HOME not set}/network/admin}"; [ -d "$d" ] || { echo "missing $d"; exit 1; }; f="$d/listener.ora"; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }; n=$(grep -ic extproc "$f"); [ "$n" = 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "noncompliant: extproc found in $f"

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, remove extproc from the listener.ora file. Instead of relying on the EXTPROC feature in Oracle to access external libraries, you can use a database directory to directly access the library files stored within the database server's file system, allowing you to execute code from those libraries within your PL/SQL code without going through a separate external process.

title: Ensure 'SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER' Is Set To 12a
description: This setting SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER configures the minimum authentication protocols clients can use to connect to database instances. Please note that the term VERSION in the parameter name refers to the version of the authentication protocol, not the version of the Oracle Database release. The last uncommented setting in sqlnet.ora must equal 12A (case-insensitive, spaces ignored). Default: 12 Reads the file from $TNS_ADMIN, or $ORACLE_HOME/network/admin when TNS_ADMIN is unset (Linux/UNIX hosts); fails when neither directory exists.
reference: CIS Oracle Database 23ai Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2.5 Ensure 'SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER' Is Set To 12a

audit.command: d="${TNS_ADMIN:-${ORACLE_HOME:?ORACLE_HOME not set}/network/admin}"; [ -d "$d" ] || { echo "missing $d"; exit 1; }; f="$d/sqlnet.ora"; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "noncompliant: $f not found"; exit 0; }; v=$(grep -Ei '^[[:space:]]*SQLNET\.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER[[:space:]]*=' "$f" | tail -n 1 | sed 's/^[^=]*=//' | tr -d ' \t\r' | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'); [ "$v" = "12A" ] && echo compliant || echo "noncompliant: ${v:-not set}"

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER to 12a.

title: Ensure 'SQLNET.ENCRYPTION_TYPES_SERVER' Is Set To AES256
description: The SQLNET.ENCRYPTION_TYPES_SERVER parameter specifies the encryption algorithms that the server enforces for database connections. reference: CIS Oracle Database 23ai Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2.9 Ensure 'SQLNET.ENCRYPTION_TYPES_SERVER' Is Set To AES256

Default: FALSE Run on the database host as the Oracle software owner with ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_SID and PATH set; connects to the CDB root with 'sqlplus -S / as sysdba' (OS authentication) so CDB_/GV$ views cover all open PDBs.

whenever sqlerror exit failure
set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off

title: Ensure 'REMOTE_LOGIN_PASSWORDFILE' Is Set To 'NONE'
description: The remote_login_passwordfile setting specifies whether or not Oracle checks for a password file during login and how many databases can use the password file. The setting should have a value of NONE or in the event you are running DR/Data Guard, EXCLUSIVE is an allowable value. Counts non-compliant GV$SYSTEM_PARAMETER rows across instances and containers; 0 is required. With a valid standby archive destination (Data Guard) the benchmark requires EXCLUSIVE instead of NONE. Default: EXCLUSIVE Run on the database host as the Oracle software owner with ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_SID and PATH set; connects to the CDB root with 'sqlplus -S / as sysdba' (OS authentication) so CDB_/GV$ views cover all open PDBs.

set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off
select count(*) from gv$system_parameter v
where upper(v.name) = 'REMOTE_LOGIN_PASSWORDFILE'
and (((select count(*) from v$archive_dest where status = 'VALID' and target = 'STANDBY') = 0 and upper(v.value) != 'NONE')

exit
EOF
) || exit 1

title: Ensure Old Password Versions Are Not Used
description: No password versions (hashes) prior to 12c should be allowed for user authentication. Run on the database host as the Oracle software owner with ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_SID and PATH set; connects to the CDB root with 'sqlplus -S / as sysdba' (OS authentication) so CDB_/GV$ views cover all open PDBs.
reference: CIS Oracle Database 23ai Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.4 Ensure Old Password Versions Are Not Used

out=$(sqlplus -S -L / as sysdba 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
whenever sqlerror exit failure
set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off
select count(*) from cdb_users c
where not regexp_like(c.password_versions, '^\s*12C\s*$')
and c.username not in ('SYS');
exit
EOF

title: Ensure All Auditable System Actions Commands Are Audited
description: Oracle defines (*) the various command categories such as DDL, DML, TCL, etc. partly deviating from the ANSI standard. However, these command categories are incomplete and only represent a part of the auditable commands. For this reason, the term "Auditable System Actions" is used in the following. This type of definition allows a flexible and future-oriented possibility to add new commands ... Counts (container, auditable action/privilege) pairs not covered by an enabled unified policy for ALL USERS with success and failure. Run on the database host as the Oracle software owner with ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_SID and PATH set; connects to the CDB root with 'sqlplus -S / as sysdba' (OS authentication) so CDB_/GV$ views cover all open PDBs.
reference: CIS Oracle Database 23ai Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.1 Ensure All Auditable System Actions Commands Are Audited

audit.command:
out=$(sqlplus -S -L / as sysdba 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
whenever sqlerror exit failure
set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off
with privs(privilege) as (
  select distinct a.privilege from dba_sys_privs a
  where a.privilege not in (select name from auditable_system_actions where component = 'Standard')
  and a.privilege not in ('INHERIT ANY PRIVILEGES')
  union
  select a.name from auditable_system_actions a where a.component = 'Standard'
  and a.name not in ('ALL','SELECT','DELETE','INSERT','UPDATE','EXECUTE','LOGON','LOGOFF')
),
cis_audit(con_id, audit_option) as (select c.con_id, ll.privilege from v$containers c, privs ll where c.open_mode = 'READ WRITE'),
audit_enabled as (
  select distinct aud.con_id, aud.audit_option from containers(audit_unified_policies) aud
  where aud.audit_option in (select privilege from privs)
  and aud.audit_option_type in ('SYSTEM PRIVILEGE','STANDARD ACTION')
  and exists (select 1 from containers(audit_unified_enabled_policies) e
    where e.success = 'YES' and e.failure = 'YES' and e.enabled_option = 'BY USER' and e.entity_name = 'ALL USERS'
    and e.policy_name = aud.policy_name and e.con_id = aud.con_id)
)
select count(*) from cis_audit c
where not exists (select 1 from audit_enabled e where e.audit_option = c.audit_option and e.con_id = c.con_id);
exit
EOF
) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Execute the following SQL statement to remediate this recommendation: ALTER AUDIT POLICY CIS_LOCAL_SYSTEM_ACTIONS ADD ACTIONS <DDL>; or ALTER AUDIT POLICY CIS_LOCAL_SYSTEM_ACTIONS ADD PRIVILEGES <DDL>; Note: If you do not have CIS_CDB_DDL_ACTIONS or CIS_PDB_DDL_ACTIONS policy, please create one using the CREATE AUDIT POLICY statement. Refer to Section 8.1 where a PL/SQL block is provided to help create or modify the audit policy to remediate this item in both container and pluggable database.

with cis_audit(con_id, audit_option) as (
  select c.con_id, ll.column_value from v$containers c, table(dbmsoutput_linesarray('LOGON','LOGOFF')) ll where c.open_mode = 'READ WRITE'),
audit_enabled as (

title: Ensure '%ANY%' Is Revoked from Unauthorized 'GRANTEE'
description: The Oracle database ANY keyword provides the user the capability to alter any item in the catalog of the database. Unauthorized grantees should not have that keyword assigned to them. Counts non-Oracle-maintained users and roles holding the privilege directly or through a role chain (CDB_SYS_PRIVS / CDB_ROLE_PRIVS); 0 is required, so every approved grantee must be reviewed and documented as an exception. Run on the database host as the Oracle software owner with ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_SID and PATH set; connects to the CDB root with 'sqlplus -S / as sysdba' (OS authentication) so CDB_/GV$ views cover all open PDBs.
reference: CIS Oracle Database 23ai Benchmark v1.1.0 - 6.1.1 Ensure '%ANY%' Is Revoked from Unauthorized 'GRANTEE'

audit.command:
out=$(sqlplus -S -L / as sysdba 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
whenever sqlerror exit failure
set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off
with nm as (
  select role as grantee from cdb_roles where oracle_maintained = 'N'
  union select username from cdb_users where oracle_maintained = 'N'
),
direct_privs as (select grantee from cdb_sys_privs where privilege like '%ANY%'),
indirect_privs as (
  select grantee from cdb_role_privs
  start with granted_role in (select p.grantee from cdb_sys_privs p, cdb_roles r where p.privilege like '%ANY%' and p.grantee = r.role)
  connect by nocycle prior grantee = granted_role
)
select count(*) from (select grantee from direct_privs union select grantee from indirect_privs) c
where c.grantee in (select grantee from nm);
exit
EOF
) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: To remediate this setting, execute the following SQL statement, keeping in mind if this is granted in both container and pluggable database, you must connect to both places to revoke. Please ensure proper impact analysis is done before revoking the privilege from a role. REVOKE <ANY Privilege> FROM <grantee>; In the case of a grant via a role : REVOKE <rolename> FROM <grantee>;

title: Ensure Critical Packages Are Audited
description: Auditing critical packages in Oracle is essential to ensure database security, maintain accountability, and support compliance with regulatory requirements. set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off

  select c.con_id, ll.column_value from v$containers c, table(dbmsoutput_linesarray('DBMS_AW','DBMS_CRYPTO','DBMS_FGA','DBMS_JAVA_TEST','DBMS_JOB','DBMS_LOGMNR','DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN','DBMS_REDACT',

  select distinct aud.con_id, aud.object_name from containers(audit_unified_policies) aud

audit.command:
out=$(sqlplus -S -L / as sysdba 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
whenever sqlerror exit failure
set heading off feedback off pagesize 0 verify off echo off trimspool on define off
with cis_audit(con_id, audit_option) as (select c.con_id, 'EXPORT' from v$containers c where c.open_mode = 'READ WRITE'),
audit_enabled as (
  select distinct aud.con_id, aud.audit_option from containers(audit_unified_policies) aud
  where aud.audit_option in ('EXPORT') and aud.audit_option_type = 'DATAPUMP ACTION'
  and exists (select 1 from containers(audit_unified_enabled_policies) e
    where e.success = 'YES' and e.failure = 'YES' and e.enabled_option = 'BY USER' and e.entity_name = 'ALL USERS'
    and e.policy_name = aud.policy_name and e.con_id = aud.con_id)
)
select count(*) from cis_audit c
where not exists (select 1 from audit_enabled e where e.audit_option = c.audit_option and e.con_id = c.con_id);
exit
EOF
) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out"
